decisions.reason: As a flagship reusable harvesting crate, it sits very close to the firm's core packaging knowledge and can be improved through its strong in-house development and engineering capabilities.
A foldable large container is central to the firm's established returnable transport packaging business, and its continued standalone presentation suggests strong fit and learnability.
A stackable plastic crate is highly related to the firm's existing crate and container expertise, so management would expect to refine rather than withdraw it.
A medium-duty rackable pallet remains within the firm's core pallet knowledge base, making it a product the firm can absorb feedback on and develop further.

The spill-retention pallet is somewhat more specialized than the firm's main logistics products, but it still builds on the firm's plastic pallet and engineering capabilities enough to justify retention.
A plastic pallet with load retainers is a related extension of the firm's pallet portfolio, and its existing manufacturing and design know-how lowers the need to drop it quickly.
